newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline steady, eyes on backwardation, barges.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline steady, eyes on backwardation, barges.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were steady in very quiet Monday action as traders zeroed in on recent buying by one trader in the barge market and the backwardation that will greet the market in May.

A noted buyer of barges last week had not yet surfaced to start this week, traders said, and any bullish repurcussions were in doubt with the arbitrage to the U.S. shut. NYMEX gasoline traded slightly lower overnight.
Some traders who capitalised on the market's contango to build up inventories may also be more willing to sell their supplies with the backwardation in May/June prices.

Prompt Eurograde barges were heard at $194/$196 fob ARA with first half May about $2 higher. May/June swaps were talked at a $2.50/$3 backwardation, with May at $195/$196.25 after a swap was heard done at $194 for April against $196.50 for first half May.

"I'm definitely not as bullish as some people were on May," one trader at a major said. "We had a nice contango in the market and now most people are waiting to sell out...If we continue to see crude in contango, we could easily see the May/June (gasoline swaps) at flat."

Signs of a potential squeeze in the ARA barge market were also overblown, since the approximate 100,000 tonnes in short positions is more than offset by the material held in storage in Amsterdam and for Rotterdam refinery material, he said.
"I feel that the barrels that are in tank are a bigger number than what the shorts have in their number," he said. "The potential squeeze players don't have enough ammunition to keep it up."
